feat(MeasureTheory): countable uncurry preserves strong measurability (#45492)
A countable family of strongly measurable functions is jointly strongly measurable when singletons in the index space are measurable.
Add `stronglyMeasurable_uncurry_of_countable` with only `[TopologicalSpace β]` on the target: no pseudometrizability, topology on the index, or measurable-space structure on the target is required. The proof directly assembles simple-function approximations, using an eventually exact finite-range approximation of the countable index.
Use the new lemma to shorten `stronglyMeasurable_uncurry_of_continuous_of_stronglyMeasurable`.
This is an independent prerequisite for #34716; it does not depend on that PR or #42164.

feat(Algebra/QuadraticAlgebra/Int): integral elements and the discriminant (#45296)
For `z` an integral element of `QuadraticAlgebra ℚ a b`, we prove that `discr a b` is the square of the denominator of `z.im` times an integer congruent to `0` or `1` modulo `4`. Conversely, if `discr a b = d ^ 2 * e` with `1 < |d|` and `e` congruent to `0` or `1` modulo `4`, we construct an integral element `z` not in `QuadraticAlgebra ℤ a b` such that `d • z` lies in it.
These are the two directions needed to determine when `QuadraticAlgebra ℤ a b` is the integral closure of `ℤ` in `QuadraticAlgebra ℚ a b`, which is done in a later PR.

feat(CategoryTheory): external products of derivability structures (#43896)
The external product of two left/right derivability structures is again a derivability structure (when one assumes that the properties of morphisms which appear contain identities).
This observation of mine (in 2023) was my main motivation for the formalization of derivability structures, because it would allow to formalize not only derived functors in one variable (see #43267), but also derived functors in several variables (like the tensor product, see https://github.com/joelriou/mathlib4/blob/jriou_localization/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Localization/DerivabilityStructure/Monoidal.lean).

feat(NumberTheory/ArithmeticFunction): prodPrimeFactors_one_sub for every n (#43749)
`IsMultiplicative.prodPrimeFactors_one_sub_of_squarefree` gives
```
∏ p ∈ n.primeFactors, (1 - f p) = ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, μ d * f d
```
only for squarefree `n`. The hypothesis is not needed: the summands with `d` not squarefree vanish (`μ d = 0`), and the squarefree divisors of `n` are exactly the divisors of `∏ p ∈ n.primeFactors, p`, which is squarefree with the same prime factors. So the general statement reduces to the squarefree one.
This PR
- adds `IsMultiplicative.prodPrimeFactors_one_sub`, the identity for every `n ≠ 0`, with the same orientation and naming as the existing lemma;
- deprecates `IsMultiplicative.prodPrimeFactors_one_sub_of_squarefree` in favour of it (as requested in review), and inlines its proof.

A new file `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/ObjectProperty/BinaryProductsClosure.lean` is also added by part of the content of `FiniteProducts.lean` in order to avoid importing set theory definitions in some algebra files.

The plan for stating that a filtration satisfies the "usual conditions" is to use the two classes `IsRightContinuous` and `IsComplete` together, without adding another class on top.

ci: run independent build-pipeline steps in parallel (#44603)
This PR runs independent steps of `build_template.yml` at the same time, with the Actions parallel-steps feature. The feature needs runner 2.335.0 or later. The self-hosted fleet is now on 2.338.x.
- `build`: the library build runs next to the Mathlib staging. The noisy-output check runs next to the library stagings.
- `upload_cache`: the artifact download runs in the background while the cache tool builds.
- `post_steps`: the declaration dump runs in the background while the other checks run.
A/B runs on `ci-dev` branches:
| Job | Stock | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Build tail, small change | 30 / 43 / 30 s | 24 / 22 / 24 s |
| Build tail, large change | 200 s | 163 s |
| Upload to cache, small change | 72 / 65 / 62 s | 52 / 56 / 47 s |
| Upload to cache, large change | 54 s | 60 s |
| Post-Build, small change | 254 / 226 / 214 s | 259 / 225 / 196 s |
| Post-Build, large change | 252 s | 198 s |
The build tail starts when the library cache fetch ends and stops when the staging check starts. In the small-change rounds, stock ran on 16-, 32- and 16-vCPU hosts, and this PR ran on 32-, 16- and 32-vCPU hosts. Both large-change runs ran on 16-vCPU hosts.
The Upload and Post-Build jobs run on GitHub-hosted runners, so their times vary more than the build tail. For example, the Mathlib cache fetch in Post-Build takes 62 to 83 s. The declaration dump takes 22 to 28 s, so the background dump saves at most that much per run.
A failed step has the same effect as in the sequential template, with two differences:
- When the noisy-output check fails, the library stagings in its group still finish.
- When the Mathlib staging fails, the job skips the three library checks and the noisy-output check. Then `RUN_TESTS` is false, and `test_lint` skips the tests. The sequential template runs these checks before the staging, so a failed staging does not stop the tests.
A cancelled run does not start the members of a parallel group, and it stops the members that run. Thus a separate step after the first group stages the Mathlib cache files of a cancelled run, as the sequential template does. `cache stage` stages only the files that it packs in the same call, so the step first deletes the `.ltar` files that are newer than a mark of `prepare staging directory`. `cache stage` then packs and stages them again.

feat(Tactic/NormCharpoly): add the `norm_charpoly` simproc and the `eval_charpoly` tactic (#44433)
add the `norm_charpoly` simproc and `eval_charpoly` tactic that normalise the characteristic polynomial of a matrix literal over a commutative ring that embeds in ℚ such as ℚ and ℤ.
```lean
example : Matrix.charpoly (R := ℤ) !![1, 2; 3, 4] = X ^ 2 - 5 * X - 2 := by
  eval_charpoly
```
The simproc `norm_charpoly` rewrites `Matrix.charpoly A` to a polynomial in the normal form of `ring_nf`. It works similar to `norm_rank` and `norm_det` by producing an untrusted computation.  In this case the computations are reduction of an input matrix to Hessenberg form (#44432) and efficient algorithm to compute characteristic polynomial from a Hessenberg matrix (#44431). 
This PR adds the tactic / meta code to certify the untrusted computations for an input matrix literal via the kernel.

feat: lemmas showing properties of ofDerivation added (#41887)
Given an `R`-Lie algebra `L` and a commutative `R`-algebra `A`, there is a Lie algebra structure on `(A ⊗[R] L)`.
A derivation of `A` induces a Lie derivation of  `(A ⊗[R] L)`, and one obtains a Lie algebra map
```
ofDerivation : Derivation R A A →ₗ⁅R⁆ LieDerivation R (A ⊗[R] L) (A ⊗[R] L)
```
In this PR we add a Lemma showing that `ofDerivation` is in fact `A`-linear, and that the resulting LieDerivation satisfies a Leibniz rule with respect to the `A`-multiplication on `A ⊗[R] L`.

feat(FieldTheory/Finite): add irreducibility criterion for polynomials over finite fields (#45286)
Add `irreducible_iff_dvd_X_pow_card_pow_sub_X_and_isCoprime` giving an irreducibility criterion for a polynomial `f` of degree `n` over a finite field with `q` elements: `f` is irreducible if and only if `f` divides `X ^ q ^ n - X` and `f` is coprime to `X ^ q ^ m - X` for every proper divisor `m` of `n`.

feat(NumberTheory/AddCharacter): the additive character attached to the trace (#44545)
Given a primitive `p`-th root of unity `ζ` in a ring `R`, and a commutative algebra `A` over `ZMod p`, this adds the additive character of `A` with values in `R` sending `x` to `ζ` raised to the trace of `x`.
The basic properties follow: the character is nontrivial, hence primitive, when `A` is a finite field, it is invariant under the Frobenius, it is compatible with extending the ring of values, and its values are congruent to `1` modulo any ideal containing `ζ - 1`.
This character will be used to construct the Gauss sums in Stickelberger's theorem.

feat(NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol): the quadratic character sum along an odd function vanishes (#44122)

refactor(Algebra/Order): unbundle group and ring cone (#37298)
* Unbundle `GroupCone` and `RingCone` using `Submonoid.IsMulPointed`
This PR deprecates the [GroupCone](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Group/Cone.html#GroupCone) and [RingCone](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Ring/Cone.html#RingCone) structures, making use of the predicates `Submonoid.IsMulPointed` and `AddSubmonoid.IsPointed` defined in that file instead.
These predicates allow us to treat uniformly
* positive cones in groups and rings
* pointed cones in vector spaces over an ordered field
* orderings in rings
This reduces duplication of theorems.
Unbundling group and ring cones is further justified by the principle that there are no new operations on them: they correspond to operations on the underlying submonoids and subsemirings, respectively. See the discussion at https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/When.20should.20subobjects.20be.20bundled.3F/with/609099816
See also #36863 for the analogous change to ring orderings.

fix(cache): time out stalled downloads and retry hard failures in a fresh pass (#45096)
`cache get` can lose a few downloads when a transfer stops early, or when a connection freezes and curl waits without a time limit. On 2026-10-27 a frozen connection held a CI job for 95 minutes on 5 of 9,080 files.
The download curl runs with `--connect-timeout 30 --speed-time 30 --speed-limit 1`. A connection setup that takes more than 30 s, or a transfer that receives no bytes for 30 s, fails with curl exit 28. curl retries a failed connection setup on a new connection. After the first pass over all cache locations, the tool retries the failed downloads once, in new `curl` processes. curl retries a timed-out transfer on the same connection. The new process of the second pass opens a new connection, which recovers the file.
A healthy get has a first-byte time under 1 s, and a slow transfer keeps its bytes flowing, so the limit trips on a frozen connection only. When every transfer fails, the second pass repeats the first, so the time to failure about doubles.
Tested against a local proxy that interrupts transfers, and against a local HTTP/2 server that leaves 3 of 94 requests unanswered on the first connection. The tool recovers in both tests and exits 1 when a failure persists. Without the stall flags it hangs in the second test.

chore(Init): stop setting a default library suggestions engine (#44323)
This PR removes the import of `Lean.LibrarySuggestions.Default` from `Mathlib.Init`. As a result, Mathlib does not set a default library suggestions engine.
The default engine makes Mathlib slow to use. Since leanprover/lean4#15159, the engine builds its index at the first query in each process. With `import Mathlib`, this index build takes minutes. The Lean maintainers consider the feature unused.
Effect on users: a file that uses the `+suggestions` mode of `grind`, `simp?`, `simp_all?` or `solve_by_elim` must select an engine, or the tactic fails. To select the default engine, add `import Lean.LibrarySuggestions.Default`. To select a different engine, use `set_library_suggestions`. `try?` works without an engine.
Other changes:
- `Mathlib.Tactic.DuplicateDecls` imports `Lean.Meta.CompletionName` directly. The removed import supplied this module transitively.
- `MathlibTest/RegisterTryTactic.lean` does not disable library suggestions. Without a default engine, this workaround has no purpose.
- The docstrings in `Mathlib.Tactic.TacticAnalysis.Declarations` use `grind` as the example tactic, not `grind +suggestions`.
Discussion: [#lean4 > lean4#15159 causes significant regression in MathlibTests](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/270676-lean4/topic/lean4.2315159.20causes.20significant.20regression.20in.20MathlibTests)
🤖

chore: replace `irreducible_def` with `no_expose` (#45063)
The `no_expose` attribute can be used in place of `irreducible_def`, and leads to easier proofs because the definition can be unfolded the file containing the definition.
Another difference is that by using `no_expose`, the definition value is not exported at all, so in downstream modules it cannot be unfolded with e.g. `rw [foo]` or `rw [foo_def]`. Instead, a public lemma like `foo_def` needs to be added explicitly. This PR does that where necessary. If there is no such lemma, but you still need access to the definition value, `import all` can be used as a workaround.
Since mathlib now enforces downstream users to use the `module` system, we don't need to worry about downstream users that don't see the effects of `no_expose`.

ci: skip the inputRev check on bump branches and PRs into them (#45382)
`bump/*` branches now live in `mathlib4` rather than `mathlib4-nightly-testing`. PRs into them, such as the `downstream-lean4` export in #45345, depend on the `nightly-testing` branches of our dependencies. The "validate lake-manifest.json inputRevs" step in `build_template.yml` runs on these branches and fails them, though it used to be skipped when the branches were in the nightly-testing repo.
This PR skips the validation step when either of these starts with `bump/`:
- `github.ref_name`: pushes to `bump/*` branches, including the automation's `bump/nightly-*` branches.
- `github.base_ref`: PRs into a `bump/*` branch, from any repo.
(Note that `head_ref` is not read, so a PR from a branch starting with `bump/` can't get around this.)
Not covered: a non-`bump/*` branch pushed to mathlib4 with a PR into a bump branch. Push builds can't see the PR's base, so the check still runs there. (No one should be creating such branches and we have branch protection rules against this.)

feat(Topology/Order): separability is hereditary for linearly ordered topological spaces (#41918)
In this PR we prove that
1. `isTopologicalBasis_isOpen_ordConnected`: in a linearly ordered topological space, every point of an open set `U` has an open `Set.OrdConnected` neighbourhood contained in `U`.
2. `countable_setOf_isolated_subtype`: in a separable linearly ordered topological space, the points of a subset `s` that are isolated in the subspace `s` form a countable set.
3. A subset of a separable linearly ordered topological space is separable in the subspace topology. This is proved as an instance.
The material was developed for showing the measurability of the pathwise variation of a continuous stochastic process in https://github.com/RemyDegenne/brownian-motion/pull/494. Created with the help of Claude Code, carefully reviewed and golfed by myself.

feat(Topology/Connected): connected subsets of finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure (#41839)
This PR proves some properties of preconnected subsets of an extended metric space in terms of their Hausdorff measure.
- The extended diameter of a preconnected set is at most its one-dimensional Hausdorff measure
- A preconnected set with finite `d`-dimensional Hausdorff measure for some `d < 1` is a subsingleton, so any set with finite such measure is totally disconnected
- A preconnected set with finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure is totally bounded.
The main tool is that the distance from a fixed base point is `1`-Lipschitz (we define it by `x => (edist a x).toReal` and `ENNReal.toReal` is necessary because `ℝ≥0∞` is not an EMetric space and blocks me from using `LipschitzOnWith`, this is also the reason why I proved some weird lemmas like `isClopen_setOf_edist_ne_top` and `IsPreconnected.edist_ne_top`), so it does not increase Hausdorff measures, and the image of a preconnected set under it is an interval whose one-dimensional Hausdorff measure is its length. Comparing the two turns distances inside the set into lower bounds for its measure.
Some of these lemmas probably should belong to a different space. Feel free to give me some suggestions on this.
In the future, I would also like to use results in this PR to prove that a preconnected, compact subset with finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure is path-connected, and this is included in TODO.

feat(Topology/MetricSpace): a Gδ subset of a Polish space is Polish (#42693)
Adds `IsGδ.polishSpace`: a Gδ subset of a Polish space is Polish, which strengthens the existing IsOpen.polishSpace.
The proof follows the outline in Anush Tserunyan's descriptive set theory notes, https://www.math.mcgill.ca/atserunyan/Teaching_notes/dst_lectures.pdf where it is attributed to A. Bernshteyn. The "usual" approach (as in Kechris's Classical Descriptive Set Theory) constructs a complete compatible metric (the "Alexandrov metric"). The approach taken here is snappier to formalize - the idea is to give a closed embeddding from the G\delta set into another Polish space, and appeal to the fact closed subsets of Polish spaces are Polish. ci: stop using the Actions cache (#45322)
This PR stops using the Actions cache in this repository, and adds a check to `actionlint.yml` that keeps it that way. Entries in the Actions cache saved by runs on the default branch potentially affect runs on every other ref that fall back to them. GitHub already stops runs of low-trust triggers such as `pull_request_target` from saving such entries, unless a workflow asks for `cache-mode: write`. But the two jobs that still restored from the cache open or push to pull requests, so it's simpler for them not to depend on it at all.
- `rm_set_option.yml` now uses an artifact instead. The restore step takes it only from earlier runs of this workflow on master started by the schedule or by hand, since pull requests can also start runs of this workflow file and upload artifacts from them.
- `lint_and_suggest_pr.yml` no longer caches pre-commit's hook environments, which only take a few seconds to set up anyways.
- `rm_set_option.yml`, the autofix job of `lint_and_suggest_pr.yml`, and the `report` job of `olean_report.yaml`, which handles PR content, set `cache-mode: none`. GitHub then refuses them any cache access, even from actions that use the cache internally.
- The new `no-actions-cache` job fails if anything under `.github/` uses `actions/cache`, turns on an action's `cache` input, uses `leanprover/lean-action` without `use-github-cache: false`, or asks for any `cache-mode` other than `read` or `none`.
- `.github/actionlint.yml` now also ignores the unknown `cache-mode` key in `.yaml` workflows, and `docs/workflows.md` mentions the new check.

ci: check the triggering run in `workflow_run` workflows (#45321)
This PR tightens the checks in the workflows triggered by `workflow_run`, so that they now also check the triggering run's event and repository.
`export_crossrefs.yml`, `nightly_detect_failure.yml` and `update_dependencies_zulip.yml` now act only on runs for pushes to this repository. `export_telemetry.yaml` also follows the fork CI, whose runs come from other repositories, so it accepts runs for `push` and `pull_request_target` events only, the two events our CI workflows use.
The concurrency groups of `export_crossrefs.yml` and `nightly_detect_failure.yml` now include the head repository. Runs that these workflows skip then never share a group with the real ones, so they can't cancel them.
`export_crossrefs.yml` also checks that the built commit is on the master **branch** and not a merely a tag named `master`. It is also split into 3 jobs, like `update_dependencies.yml` in #44881:
- `export` runs the Lean code with only `contents: read` and no cache access, and uploads `crossrefs.json` as an artifact.
- `publish` gets the `crossref-exports` environment and the app token, and runs no code from the checkout.
- `report_failure` posts the Zulip message when either job fails.
`update_dependencies_zulip.yml` now passes the `parse_changes` output to its scripts through `env` instead of writing it into the script text. `monitor-success` also gets the same repository check as `monitor-failures`.

feat(CategoryTheory): the category of inserters (#45273)
Given `F G : C ⥤ D`, we define `Inserter F G` as the category of morphisms `F.obj X ⟶ G.obj X` for some object `X` in `C`. We also give the bare minimum API for this category: 
- the projection functor `Inserter F G ⥤ C` with a `ReflectsIsomorphism` and `Faithful` instance;
- a constructor for isomorphisms;
- a bundling of the structure map as a natural transformation `proj F G ⋙ F ⟶ proj F G ⋙ G`.
Inserters form a basic building block for a class of bicategorical limits (PIE-limits). By showing that categories of inserts are accessible when `C` and `D` and `F` and `G` are accessible, one can show that (co)-algebras for endofunctors (which are special cases of inserters) are also accessible.
This PR is part of a series of PR that formalizes the fact that one can induce accessibility (and later on local presentability) along accessible monadic right adjoints with an accessible codomain.

ci: push style fixes automatically and remove `bot fix style` (#44573)
This PR merges `pre-commit.yml` into `lint_and_suggest_pr.yml` so that all automatic style fixes are pushed to the PR by pre-commit.ci lite, and removes the `bot fix style` command, which has not worked since 2025.
On every PR, including drafts, the job now runs `lint-style-action` in its new `fix-worktree` mode (leanprover-community/lint-style-action#13: `mk_all`, `lint-style --fix` and `lint-bib.sh`, with the results left in the working tree), then the `pre-commit` hooks, and then `pre-commit-ci/lite-action`. Both sets of fixes arrive as a single `[pre-commit.ci lite]` commit, which replaces the reviewdog suggestions. Its message names the commands that changed something, such as `[pre-commit.ci lite] lake exe mk_all; lake exe lint-style --fix`, so that contributors can see how to make the same fixes locally.
Other changes:
- A per-PR concurrency group, with the lite action on `success() || failure()` rather than `always()`, so that a run superseded by a newer push cannot push stale fixes.
- The workflow's token is read-only, since the job builds code from the PR and nothing in it needs to write any more.
- The `.lean`/`.md` file-extension check moves to its own job, so that its failure cannot stop the fixes from being pushed.
- `pre-commit.yml`'s `push` trigger goes away, because the lite action only acts on `pull_request`.
- `bot_fix_style.yaml` is deleted. It was the last user of `lint-style-action`'s `fix` mode, which was removed upstream in leanprover-community/lint-style-action#12. It also started a no-op run on every comment and review in the repository.
- `style_lint` in `build_template.yml` moves to the same `lint-style-action` version, so the repository has a single pin and nothing uses the `mathlib4-compat` branch any more. `actions/checkout` v7 refuses fork PR code under `pull_request_target`, and the action's own checkout has no way to opt in. So the job now checks out `pr_branch_ref` itself, the same way `post_steps` does (`allow-unsafe-pr-checkout`, no persisted credentials), and passes `checkout: false`.
The commit messages have the details, including the evidence that `bot fix style` has been broken since lint-style-action 5f18958.

```
When `pp.mdata` is set to true, expressions with mdata are printed by first printing the mdata and the printing the bare expression underneath. This breaks `@[pp_with_univ]` which works by applying mdata setting `pp.universes` to true onto the constant name, and then redelaborating the new expression containing mdata. This causes an infinite loop the the delaborator since `@[pp_with_univ]` applies the mdata, and then since `pp.mdata` is true the mdata is removed before delaborating the constant, which then has mdata applied again, and so on. We fix the issue by instead having the implementation of `@[pp_with_univ]` directly set the `pp.universes` option, instead of delegating it to `delabMData` with a metadata.

fix(build): let the toolchain select Lake linkage (#45209)

```text

uncaught exception: failed to load Lake workspace
```
The Lean toolchain specified in Mathlib’s `lean-toolchain` file already supplies `-lLake -lLeanExport` for static linking and `-lLake_shared` for shared linking ([source](https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/blob/c9afcddf514a6772bd4d649f7cfc04eff0b9f15e/src/CMakeLists.txt#L508-L514)). The regression came from [Lean #14885](https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/pull/14885), which added a `LeanExport` dependency to Lake. With the explicit static `-lLake`, unresolved `LeanExport` initializers are taken from `libLake_shared.dll`, loading a second copy of Lake and duplicating initialization. Previously the unused DLL was omitted. [Lean #14963](https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/pull/14963) added `-lLeanExport` to the automatic static flags, but Windows interpreter executables use the shared flags, so Mathlib's explicit override still causes this mixture. The old overrides originated in [Mathlib #13850](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/13850).

fix(tactic): skip implementation-detail declarations in `specialize_all` (#44379)
This commit fixes a bug in the `specialize_all` tactic that causes incorrect behavior in `specialize_all; assumption`.
In the original implementation of `specialize_all`, the statement `for h in ← getLCtx do` iterates over the entire local context without filtering out auxiliary declarations, particularly the theorem currently being proved. This allows the subsequent `assumption` tactic to directly use the local hypothesis produced by specializing that declaration, recursively “proving” the current theorem. This issue makes `tauto_set` unusable in many cases where it successfully executes `specialize_all` internally.
Here are some examples of the bug in `specialize_all` (before the fix):
```lean
import Mathlib.Tactic.TautoSet
/-- error: fail to show termination for
  _example
with errors
failed to infer structural recursion:
Cannot use parameter x:
  failed to eliminate recursive application
    _example x✝ rfl -/
#guard_msgs (substring := true) in
example (x : ℕ) : {x} ⊆ Set.univ := by tauto_set
/-- error: fail to show termination for
  _example -/
#guard_msgs (substring := true) in
example {α : Type} : α → False := by
  intro x
  specialize_all x
  assumption
```
This issue does not cause Lean to accept the invalid proof, because it is rejected by the termination checker.
I fixed this issue by adding
```lean
unless h.isImplementationDetail do
```
after the loop statement above to filter out all implementation-detail hypotheses, including the auxiliary declaration for the current theorem. I also added three regression tests in `MathlibTest/Tactic/TautoSet.lean`. All three compile successfully now, but fail with `error: fail to show termination for ...` before the fix.
GPT-6-Astra was used to help locate the bug and translate the PR description to English.

feat(NumberTheory/ModularForms): evaluation at E₄, E₆ surjectively maps onto level-1 graded ring (#39258)
Defines the evaluation homomorphism `evalE₄E₆ : ℂ[X₀, X₁] →ₐ[ℂ] ⨁ k, ModularForm 𝒮ℒ k` (`X₀ ↦ E₄`, `X₁ ↦ E₆`) and proves that it is surjective: every level-one modular form is a polynomial in `E₄` and `E₆`. Also adds the equivalent statement that `E₄` and `E₆` generate the graded ring as a `ℂ`-algebra, and the resulting `Algebra.FiniteType` and `IsNoetherianRing` instances. First half of #38813.
The proof is one induction on the weight `k`. Forms of negative or odd weight, or of weight `2`, vanish. Otherwise `k = 4a + 6b`, and subtracting the right multiple of `E₄ᵃE₆ᵇ` from a form of weight `k` leaves a cusp form. That cusp form is `Δ` times a form of weight `k - 12` (`CuspForm.discriminantEquiv`), and `Δ = (E₄³ - E₆²) / 1728` (`discriminant_eq_E₄_cube_sub_E₆_sq_graded`). The same step covers the weights below `12`, so there is no separate small-weight case analysis.
The material is appended to `Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/LevelOne/GradedRing.lean`, next to the identity for `Δ` that it uses.
## Main results
- `ModularForm.evalE₄E₆`
- `ModularForm.evalE₄E₆_surjective`
- `ModularForm.adjoin_E₄_E₆_eq_top`
- instances `Algebra.FiniteType ℂ (⨁ k, ModularForm 𝒮ℒ k)` and `IsNoetherianRing (⨁ k, ModularForm 𝒮ℒ k)`

ci: run `lake update` in a job without credentials (#44881)
This PR splits `update_dependencies.yml` into 3 jobs. 
First, it moves `lake update` into a job without credentials. This is needed because `lake update` runs code from the new dependency revisions (their lakefiles and any `post_update` hooks) before anyone has reviewed them. The job that runs it now has only `contents: read`, no cache access, no secrets, and no persisted git credentials. It uploads `lake-manifest.json` and `lean-toolchain` as an artifact.
A second job, `update-pr`, does everything that needs the app token: bumping the `mathlib-ci` pin, working out the PR state, and creating or updating the PR. It doesn't run any code from the dependencies. If `lean-toolchain` changed, it skips the PR, as before. Otherwise it takes only `lake-manifest.json` from the artifact and checks that it is well formed. It then accepts only revision changes: every other field must match master's manifest, except that a transitive package's `inputRev` may change along with its parent's manifest. If an upstream change legitimately does more, such as adding a dependency or moving a repository, the run fails with the difference in its log, and that update has to be done by hand. `create-pull-request` now gets `add-paths`, so the PR only ever changes `lake-manifest.json` and the `mathlib-ci` pin. 
The third and final job contains the Zulip failure message and it runs when either of the other jobs fails.
One behavior change: `lake update` now also runs while the PR is labelled `ready-to-merge`. Its result is discarded, since nothing is pushed in that state.
`.github/actionlint.yml` ignores the `cache-mode` key, which actionlint 1.7.12 doesn't know yet (rhysd/actionlint#745).

feat(RingTheory/FractionalIdeal): add HasUniqueRoots instance (#40636)
- The monoid of fractional ideals with respect to `S ≤ R⁰` is the localization of the monoid of ideals of `R` at the principal ideals generated by an element of `S`.
- The target of a localization map of a monoid with unique roots has unique roots.
- As a consequence, the monoid of fractional ideals has unique roots when the monoid of ideals does.
A comment also records that the monoid of ideals of a Dedekind domain has unique roots only once `Mathlib.Algebra.GroupWithZero.Torsion` is imported.
:robot: This PR was extracted from the [SKW project](https://github.com/xroblot/SKW) by Claude.

feat(Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Metric): add distance lemmas for graph maps (#44872)
Graph homomorphisms map walks to walks of the same length, so they do not increase extended graph distance. For natural-valued distance, the corresponding bound requires source reachability because unreachable pairs use the junk value `0`.
Add:
- `SimpleGraph.Hom.edist_le`
- `SimpleGraph.Iso.edist_eq`
- `SimpleGraph.Hom.dist_le`
- `SimpleGraph.Iso.dist_eq`
Mark both isomorphism equalities as `@[simp]`. Refactor the existing distance-antitonicity results for graph inclusions through `Hom.ofLE`, making them special cases of the homomorphism bounds.
Discussed on Zulip: [distance and balls under graph maps](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/252551-graph-theory/topic/distance.20and.20balls.20under.20graph.20maps/with/631709959).

feat(Linter/Style): lint against `∀ᵉ`/`∃ᵉ` (#44544)
The `∀ᵉ`/`∃ᵉ` notation is used rarely in mathlib, so to many users it is an unfamiliar notation. Therefore, it would be better to simply not use it.
This PR adds a linter against the notation, which comes with a `Try this` suggestions that replaces the notation with uses of plain `∀`/`∃`
- The adaptations have been generated fully automatically using these `Try this` suggestions. So, it is easiest to review this PR commit by commit.
- The `∃ᵉ` notation is still used in one place, namely in the macro that defines the `{_ | _}` notation for sets. The linter explicitly does not flag this.
- This linter would fit in very nicely into the framework of #44496. That can be done in a follow-up PR after that is merged, and will remove the slowdown that this PR adds.

feat(NumberTheory/EllipticDivisibilitySequence): prove that a normalised elliptic divisibility sequence is an elliptic sequence (#42453)
This is the updated version of #13155 and contains the proof that a sequence satisfying the even and odd elliptic relations (with mild additional conditions) is an elliptic net and hence an elliptic sequence. This is the main argument in [Section 2 of Junyan's paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.05280). Previously it was broken down into hundreds of lines of multiple lemmas but I was able to condense it into a single lemma with multiple `wlog`s that are hopefully self-explanatory.

This PR adds four lemmas  in Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Ring.lean, placed in the fractional-part section, complementing the existing one-sided bounds le_floor_add and le_floor_add_floor.
Here are the lemmas:
 
* floor_add_eq — writes ⌊a + b⌋ exactly as ⌊a⌋ + ⌊b⌋ + ⌊fract a + fract b⌋
* floor_add_eq_add_iff — the floors add exactly ⟺ the fractional parts sum below 1
* floor_add_eq_add_add_one_iff — the +1 case ⟺ the fractional parts sum to at least 1
* floor_add_eq_or — the dichotomy: it's always one or the other
The library has the two inequalities but not the exact case analysis, and this closes that small gap. In addition, these are the lemmas for the mechanical/Beatty-word development proposed here --https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/Sturmian.20.28mechanical.29.20words/near/610836902.
Claude helped draft the Lean code; I reviewed the code, built the module locally, and it compiled.

chore(RingTheory/Pochhammer): fix the type of ascPochhammer_eval_succ (#42827)
The existing two theorems have the following signature
```lean4
theorem ascPochhammer_nat_eval_succ (r n : ℕ) : 
    n * Polynomial.eval (n + 1) (ascPochhammer ℕ r) = (n + r) * Polynomial.eval n (ascPochhammer ℕ r)
theorem ascPochhammer_eval_succ (S : Type*) [Semiring S] (r n : ℕ) : 
    ↑n * Polynomial.eval (↑n + 1) (ascPochhammer S r) = (↑n + ↑r) * Polynomial.eval (↑n) (ascPochhammer S r)
```
However what's more useful in practice is the following
```lean4
theorem ascPochhammer_eval_succ {S : Type*} [Semiring S] (r : ℕ) (n : S) : 
    n * Polynomial.eval (n + 1) (ascPochhammer S r) =  Polynomial.eval n (ascPochhammer S r) * (n + ↑r)
```
which this PR proves. Note that the multiplication order is changed so it doesn't require commutativity on S.
The old `ascPochhammer_nat_eval_succ` is now a specialization of the new `ascPochhammer_eval_succ` with `S = ℕ` & mul_comm, so it is redundant, thus deprecated.

feat(Analysis/Polynomial): the sign of a polynomial immediately to the right of a point (#44248)
This PR defines `Polynomial.signRight x p : SignType`, the sign that a real polynomial `p` takes
on a sufficiently small interval `(x, x + ε)`, as the limit of `sign (p.eval y)` as `y → x` from the right, and
develops its basic API:
* `eventually_sign_eq_signRight`, `signRight_eq_iff`: the defining property and its uniqueness;
* `signRight_eq_zero_iff`: `signRight x p = 0` iff `p = 0`;
* `signRight_mul`, `signRight_neg`, `signRight_C`: `signRight x` is multiplicative, commutes with
  negation and agrees with `SignType.sign` on constants;
* `signRight_of_eval_ne_zero`, `signRight_of_eval_eq_zero`: the computation rule
  `signRight x p = sign (p.eval x)` if `p.eval x ≠ 0`, and `signRight x p = signRight x (derivative p)`
  otherwise (via the mean value theorem).
This is the local invariant behind Sturm's theorem: it determines the direction in which the sign
of a Sturm sequence changes across a root, and it will be used to define the Cauchy index in the
next PR of the series.
This is the third PR of a series formalising the Sturm–Tarski theorem, following #43783
(`List.signVariations`) and #43954 (`Polynomial.sturmSeq`). Everything is stated over `ℝ`; the
statements hold over any real closed field, and the implementation notes record what is needed to
generalise them.

fix(NumberTheory/ModularForms/LFunction): correct the value of `L` at `s = 0` (#44547)
`ModularForm.L hk f s := Λ hk f s * (2 / Gammaℂ s)` is `0` at `s = 0` for every modular form, because `Gammaℂ 0 = 0`. But when `valueAtInfty f ≠ 0`, the completed function `Λ hk f` has a simple pole at `0` with residue `-valueAtInfty f` (`WeakFEPair.Λ_residue_zero`), which cancels the zero of `1 / Gammaℂ`. So the L-function has a removable singularity at `0` with value `-valueAtInfty f`, and the current `L hk f` is discontinuous there. For the normalised Eisenstein series `E₄`, `L hk E₄ 0 = 0` while `L hk E₄ s → -1` as `s → 0`; classically `L(E₄, 0) = 240 ζ(0) ζ(-3) = -1`.
This PR follows the treatment of the same removable singularity for `hurwitzZetaEven` / `riemannZeta`:
- `L` is now `Function.update (fun s ↦ Λ hk f s * (2 / Gammaℂ s)) 0 (-valueAtInfty f)`, and its docstring explains the value at `0`.
- New lemmas: `ModularForm.L_of_ne_zero`, `ModularForm.L_apply_zero` (`@[simp]`), `ModularForm.tendsto_L_nhdsNE_zero`, `ModularForm.continuousAt_L_zero` (`@[fun_prop]`).
- New lemma `Complex.Gammaℂ_residue_zero`, the analogue of `Complex.Gammaℝ_residue_zero`.
- The proofs of `hasSum_L` (via `hasSum_L_of_hasSum_Λ`) and `CuspForm.differentiable_L` are adjusted. For cusp forms `valueAtInfty f = 0`, so `L` is pointwise unchanged; away from `0` it is unchanged for every form.

Currently the API for simplifying expressions of the form `(PiTensorProduct.reindex ...).symm ...` is limited, with the primary existing tool being:
```
/-- This lemma is impractical to state in the dependent case. -/
@[simp]
theorem reindex_symm (e : ι ≃ ι₂) :
    (reindex R (fun _ ↦ M) e).symm = reindex R (fun _ ↦ M) e.symm := by ...
```
To help simplify expressions of this form (particularly in the dependent case where each factor need not be the same module), this PR provides two new theorems:
```
theorem reindex_symm_tprod (e : ι ≃ ι₂) (f : Π i, s i) :
    (reindex R s e).symm (tprod R (fun i ↦ f (e.symm i))) = tprod R f
theorem reindex_symm_symm_tprod (e : ι₂ ≃ ι) (f : Π i, s i) :
    (reindex R s e.symm).symm (tprod R (fun i ↦ f (e i))) = tprod R f
```
I (Daniel) am not actually convinced that the statement of `reindex_symm` is true in the dependent case (as the docstring implies), but I have left it alone in-case I am missing something.

feat(Cache): set the number of parallel downloads with `MATHLIB_CACHE_PARALLEL_MAX` (#44615)
The new variable `MATHLIB_CACHE_PARALLEL_MAX` sets the number of simultaneous transfers in `cache get`. Without the variable, `cache get` passes no flag, so curl uses its default of 50 or a `parallel-max` line in `~/.curlrc`. CI reads the value from the GitHub variable of the same name, which is 150 in mathlib4 and mathlib4-nightly-testing.
A file that the cache does not hold costs one round trip, so a pass over many such files takes about (file count / transfers) round trips. `cache get` on a branch tries the master cache first. When the branch changes a file that most of Mathlib imports, almost every file misses there. A real `cache get` with a full miss (9007 files) took 70.3 s with 50 transfers and 34.6 s with 150.
The GH variable is currently set to 150, so it will apply after this PR is merged. Each transfer holds an output file and can hold its own connection. The self-hosted CI runners have a soft open-file limit of 1024, and the GitHub-hosted runners have a higher limit.

feat(Algebra/MvPolynomial): compact either summand of a sum of variables (#42203)
Currently `exists_fin_rename` reindexes the entire variable type along an injection `Fin n → σ`. At `σ ⊕ τ` this renumbers the variables of both summands together, so it cannot be used when one summand carries meaning that has to be preserved.
This PR adds variants that compact only one summand and leave the other alone, mirroring the existing `exists_finset_rename` / `exists_fin_rename` pair:
```lean
theorem exists_finset_right_rename (p : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ τ) R) :
    ∃ (t : Finset τ) (q : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ t) R), p = q.rename (Sum.map id (↑))
theorem exists_finset_left_rename (p : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ τ) R) :
    ∃ (t : Finset σ) (q : MvPolynomial (t ⊕ τ) R), p = q.rename (Sum.map (↑) id)
theorem exists_fin_right_rename (p : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ τ) R) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → τ) (_hf : Injective f) (q : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ Fin n) R),
      p = q.rename (Sum.map id f)
theorem exists_fin_left_rename (p : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ τ) R) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → σ) (_hf : Injective f) (q : MvPolynomial (Fin n ⊕ τ) R),
      p = q.rename (Sum.map f id)
```
`exists_finset_right_rename` factors `exists_finset_rename` through `Finset.toRight`: rename along the map that fixes the left-hand variables and sends each right-hand variable of the finset into `s.toRight`. `exists_finset_left_rename` follows from it by swapping the summands with `Equiv.sumComm`. The `Fin` versions then enumerate the finset with `Fintype.equivFin`, the same way that `exists_fin_rename` does.
Motivation: a Diophantine relation is presented as a polynomial in input variables along with existentially quantified witness variables, and the normal form wants inputs indexed by `Fin n` and witnesses compacted to `Fin m`. Only the witnesses may be reindexed; renumbering the inputs changes the relation being represented. This comes up in work I've been exploring towards Hilbert's tenth problem (the TODO in `Mathlib.NumberTheory.Dioph`), though the statements are independent of that.
🤖 These proofs were written with the assistance of Claude Opus 5 high and reviewed by GPT Sol 5.6 xhigh; the final proofs follow the reviewer's suggestions.

This PR extends the unused tactic linter to also lint for redundant uses of the `<;>` combinator. In particular, if `<;>` generates at most 1 new goal, then it is redundant, because it can be replaced with `;` or just removed entirely.
The UnnecessarySeqFocus linter in batteries also lints the same exact thing (but the code is much longer than the few lines added in this PR). So, this PR turns it off in mathlib, which gives a big speedup.
- The linter currently can't tell the difference between when `<;>` is actually unused, or only used in a way that can be replaced with `;`. I think this is acceptable, as the main goal of the linter is to point out that something is wrong.
- It turns out that the batteries linter wasn't actually imported in `Mathlib.Init`, but only in `Mathlib.Tactic.Common` (transitively via `Batteries.Tactic.Basic`). So, this PR makes this feature available in more of mathlib, and has to make some adaptations.

ci: build Archive, Counterexamples and Wanted in one lake build (#44650)
This PR builds Archive, Counterexamples and Wanted with one `lake build` in the `build` job. feat(CategoryTheory/ObjectProperty): closure properties of orthogonals and S. E. Dickson's theorem (#44226)
We study how the closure properties of a property of objects `P` interact with the
orthogonal complements `P.leftOrthogonal` and `P.rightOrthogonal`, and with passage to the
opposite category.
New file `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/ObjectProperty/OrthogonalClosed.lean`:
* In a category with zero morphisms, `P.leftOrthogonal` is closed under quotients and under
  colimits of any shape, and dually `P.rightOrthogonal` is closed under subobjects and under
  limits of any shape. These are registered as instances.
* In a preadditive balanced category, both orthogonals are closed under extensions, using the
  kernel and cokernel supplied by a short exact sequence.
* In a well-powered abelian category with coproducts, if `P` is closed under quotients,
  extensions and coproducts, then `P.rightOrthogonal.leftOrthogonal = P`
  (`ObjectProperty.leftOrthogonal_rightOrthogonal_eq_self`). The proof takes the largest
  `P`-subobject `A` of `X` (an `sSup` of subobjects) and shows the cokernel of `A ⟶ X` lies in
  `P.rightOrthogonal`, so that `A ⟶ X` is an epimorphism when `X` is in the double orthogonal.
  This is the hard direction of Dickson's characterisation of torsion classes; the instances
  above give the easy direction.
Opposite categories, in `EpiMono.lean` and `Extensions.lean`:
* `P.op` is closed under quotients iff `P` is closed under subobjects, and dually
  (`isClosedUnderQuotients_op_iff`, `isClosedUnderSubobjects_op_iff`), with `unop` versions.
* `P.op` is closed under extensions iff `P` is (`isClosedUnderExtensions_op_iff`), with an
  `unop` version.
* The forward directions are registered as instances.
Both files gain an import of `ObjectProperty.Opposite`.
This is preparatory work for torsion theories (see #36744).

fix(Translate): improve translation heuristic (#44266)
This PR improves the translation heuristic in `to_additive`/`to_dual`. In particular, the function `shouldTranslate` is changed so that instead of recursing into all subexpressions, it only visits at most one argument in an application. This fixes the problem of constants not being translated because `shouldTranslate` returned false because it found some unapplied constant.
This has several benefits:
- The function `shouldTranslate` doesn't need to visit so many expressions, so it doesn't need to use a cache anymore, and runs more quickly.
- `to_dual_ignore_args`/`to_additive_ignore_args` are not needed anymore and can be deprecated.
- We teach `to_dual` to not translate morphisms in `Type u`, because `Type u` is a fixed type. Previously, we couldn't do this because it would make the heuristic misfire. To make this work, we have to set `(relevant_arg := _)` in `FreeGroup`: this makes sense because `FreeGroup` can translate to `FreeAddGroup` no matter what the used type is.
The reasoning behind the `shouldTranslate` heuristic is as follows. If the constant already has a translation, then we know the `relevant_arg`, and we know that it is translated if and only if this relevant argument is translated. So, we only need to check that argument for whether it is translated. If the constant is not translated, we assume that the first argument is the relevant argument. This default is sensible for types like `Option α` and `α × β`: we translate it if and only if we translate `α`. If it should not be the first argument, this can be set manually with e.g. `to_additive self (relevant_arg := 2)`, and we also have `to_dual_do_translate` and `to_dual_dont_translate` to indicate that we should always/never translate that type.

feat(Analysis/Fourier): decay of the Fourier transform of a function with integrable derivatives (#42933)
If `f : ℝ → E` is `C^n` and its first `n` derivatives are integrable, then `𝓕 f` decays like `|u| ^ (-n)`.  Specifically, `Real.one_add_pow_mul_norm_fourier_le` states that
```
(1 + |u| ^ n) * ‖𝓕 f u‖ ≤ (∫ v, ‖f v‖) + ((2 * π) ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ v, ‖iteratedDeriv n f v‖
```
which, unlike a bound of the shape `‖u‖ ^ n * ‖𝓕 f u‖ ≤ C`, is also nontrivial at `u = 0`, and so can be used to deduce integrability of `𝓕 f`.  The case `n = 2` is recorded separately as `Real.one_add_sq_mul_norm_fourier_le`, in terms of `1 + u ^ 2`.  Also included is `Real.norm_fourier_le_integral_norm`, the `𝓕`-level form of `VectorFourier.norm_fourierIntegral_le_integral_norm`.  (This will be useful in a future PR of the prime number theorem.)
Mathlib already implies a decay bound of this kind, via `Real.pow_mul_norm_iteratedFDeriv_fourier_le` with `k = 0`, but with a lossy constant, a sum over all lower-order derivatives, and no content at `u = 0`.
A higher-dimensional analogue holds by the same argument, but needs a reverse bound for `fourierPowSMulRight`, for which mathlib currently only has the `≤` direction; this is left to a future PR.

chore: extend L^p lemmas from normed spaces to enormed setting (#43834)
In the refactor of eLpNorm in #42406, I adapted some lemmas in `LpSemiNorm.CompareExp` to the new setting by adding a continuity assumption. It turns out that this assumption is too strong for some applications in Carleson. This PR proves more general versions of the lemmas, suitable for Carleson.
The lemmas are of the form `eLpNorm (fun x => b (f x) (g x)) r μ ≤ c * eLpNorm f p μ * eLpNorm g q μ` when `‖b (f x) (g x)‖ ≤ c * ‖f x‖ * ‖g x‖` (where the norm could also be an nnnorm or an enorm). They were only proved in normed spaces. The PR proves versions in enormed spaces. The main new application is the inequality `eLpNorm (f * g) r μ ≤ eLpNorm f p μ * eLpNorm g q μ` when `f` and `g` take values in ENNReal.
I tried to be coherent, with lemmas named `..._of_pos` when they assume that `r` is positive, with `of_enorm` when the assumption is in terms of enorms, and `of_norm` when it's in terms of norms. Now, the main statements are the enorms ones, and the other statements are deduced from the enorms ones. I have not removed any statement, but I have renamed those that were not following this convention. The PR is maybe hard to review because of this, but the changes are mostly mechanical. I have tried hard to avoid measurability assumptions when they were not necessary.

ci: cache the MathlibTest oleans on R2 (#44301)
The `test mathlib` step in `Test and lint` builds all 416 MathlibTest files on every run. The cache tool accepts MathlibTest oleans, but CI does not stage or upload them, so the cache holds none.
This PR caches them on R2:
1. When `test` runs, `Test and lint` first fetches the MathlibTest oleans that the cache holds, with `cache get 'MathlibTest.+'`. `test` then rebuilds only the other test files.
2. After `test`, `Test and lint` stages the MathlibTest oleans that `test` built into the artifact `cache-staging-test`. Only runs that write the `master` container (`master`, `staging`, and `v4.*` tags) stage them. A test file that fails leaves no build output, so `stage` skips it.
3. A new job, `upload_test_cache`, uploads that artifact to the public R2 bucket, where `upload_cache` writes the `master` container. It uses the environment and permissions of `upload_cache`, and repeats its setup steps through YAML aliases. It uploads only when its own trust dispatch also selects the `master` container.
Other runs read the test files from `master` and upload none, because they read their own container only at their own commit.
The fetch, stage, and upload steps are `continue-on-error`, and so is the `upload_test_cache` job. A failed fetch or upload only makes `test` rebuild more files. No other job needs `upload_test_cache`, and bors does not wait for it.
`Test and lint` runs the PR's code, so it gets no upload credentials. The new steps call the `cache` binary as the build job does, with the trusted toolchain first on `PATH`. The PR's code can write to `pr-branch/.lake/` before both steps, so the fetch and stage steps run in landrun. The fetch uses the sandbox of `get-cache`. A check step fails `Test and lint` if the staging directory holds anything but regular files.
The staged set also holds the 11 ProofWidgets modules that some tests import. No other cache step stages them.

feat(cache): build the URLs of reads and uploads from a single Location type (#44173)
This PR adds one type, `Location`, that builds the URLs of every cache read and every upload (`Cache/Location.lean`). A location is a root URL, a label, and an optional scope (a repo and, optionally, a commit). The scope gives the files directory. Only a scope with a commit gives a marker.
A known container resolves to a location with `Container.location`, which adds the container segment to the base URL. A user-supplied URL resolves with `Location.ofEndpoint`. Both trim whitespace and trailing slashes.
- A read resolves its trust-ordered locations (`readLocations`), then downloads through them (`downloadFiles`).
- An upload resolves one location (`uploadLocation`), then writes the files and the location's marker, if any.
`mkFileURL`, `markerReadURL`, `StagedUploadDest`, `containerUploadDest`, `Container.getURL`, and `Cache/Upload/Dest.lean` are removed. The URLs do not change.
Behavior changes:
- All Git lookups (HEAD, `--scope` refs, `cache query`, `--unsafe`) run in the Mathlib checkout, not the current directory.
- `MATHLIB_CACHE_PUT_URL` is normalized, and upload messages label it by the variable name.
- The curl upload message names the full directory.
- `get` resolves its locations before it checks for missing files, so a bad `MATHLIB_CACHE_FROM` always warns.
The layout rules stay as they are on master. #43900 and #43330 will build on this type.
`lake exe cache-test` passes (380 assertions).

ci(cache): bound the snapshot run lookup by creation date (#44171)
The `get-cache` action picks a master `build.yml` run and downloads its `cache-snapshot` artifact to warm the local cache.
GitHub returns at most 1,000 runs for a filtered run search. When more runs match, the answer can omit every recent run. The run queries in `get-cache` have no date range, so they match thousands of runs. A Build job can then warm from a run that is months old, or get no warm start because the artifact of that run has expired.
This PR makes these changes:
- Each run query has a `created` range that starts at the retention cutoff. The range in `newest_before` ends at the merge-base date, so the first result is the correct run.
- `has_snapshot` rejects an artifact after its `expires_at` date.
- `has_snapshot` logs the artifact dates of each run that it checks.
- `gh api` prints an error response on stdout. The `api` wrapper discards the output of a failed call, so an error response does not become a run-id.
🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

refactor(Algebra/Group): fix the definition of torsion-free non-abelian groups (#42407)
This PR redefines torsion-free to be that exponentiation by every non-zero element `n : ℕ` is injective on commuting elements (i.e., `a * b = b * a → a ^ n = b ^ n → a = b`).
For commutative monoids, this is equivalent to `a ^ n = b ^ n → a = b`.
For groups, this is equivalent to `a ^ n = 1 → a = 1`.
Thus, this definition reconciles the notions of torsion-free for groups and commutative semigroups.
This definition was taken from this mathoverflow answer: https://mathoverflow.net/a/377268/95685
Zulip thread: [#mathlib4 > Definition of `IsMulTorsionFree`](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/Definition.20of.20.60IsMulTorsionFree.60/with/614317763)

feat(Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex): pullbacks and pushouts of short exact sequences (#44229)
Given a short complex `S` and a morphism `f : Y ⟶ S.X₃`, this PR constructs the short complex
`S.pull f`, namely `S.X₁ ⟶ pullback f S.g ⟶ Y`, and shows that it is short exact whenever `S` is,
in an abelian category. Dually, for `f : S.X₁ ⟶ Y` it constructs `S.push f`, namely
`Y ⟶ pushout f S.f ⟶ S.X₃`, and shows that it is short exact whenever `S` is.
In `Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/Pullback.lean`:
* `ShortComplex.pull`, with instances `Epi (S.pull f).g` (abelian, `S.g` epi) and
  `Mono (S.pull f).f` (`S.f` mono);
* `ShortComplex.ShortExact.pull`.
In `Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/Pushout.lean`:
* `ShortComplex.push`, with instances `Mono (S.push f).f` (abelian, `S.f` mono) and
  `Epi (S.push f).g` (`S.g` epi);
* `ShortComplex.ShortExact.push`.
This replaces an earlier version phrased in terms of the `Subobject` API, following a suggestion
of @joelriou, who wrote the `pull` construction.

ci: run `cache get` inside landrun after PR code has run (#44325)
In the self-hosted `build` and `test_lint` jobs, PR code can write to `pr-branch/.lake/` from the "download dependencies" step onward. That step runs `lake env`, which evaluates the PR's lakefile. Two later steps ran the trusted `cache get` outside landrun in `pr-branch/`:
- "Fetch cache from remote" in the `get-cache` action, in both jobs.
- "fetch archive, counterexamples and wanted cache", in `build`.
`leantar` follows a symlinked parent directory when it writes a file. The `rm -rf .lake/build/lib/lean/Mathlib` in "Fetch cache from remote" also follows one. Thus a directory symlink under `.lake/` sent these writes and deletions to any path that the runner user can write. The effect stays inside the job container, which is discarded after the job, and the job token is read-only. This change is hardening. It does not fix a known exploit.
Both steps now run `cache get` inside landrun with network access. landrun gives write access only to `.lake/` and the local cache directory, so a write through such a symlink fails.
Two alternatives do not work. `cache get` cannot run before "download dependencies", because it hashes the dependency sources that this step fetches. A symlink check before each step is not sufficient, because a background process from an earlier step can create the link after the check.
New comments state the sandbox rule for the `build` job and why no PR code can change `cache-staging/`. The comment on the prune step gives the correct reason why that step runs outside landrun.

feat: use requiresModuleSystem in mathlib (#41950)
This option causes a warning in any project depending on a version of mathlib containing this PR that does not use the module system. The warning can be turned off using the `allowNonModules` option in the downstream project. (We do so for `MathlibTest`, because some tests intentionally use non-modules.)
For clarity, this does not immediately cause any breakage: it is giving advance notice of potential changes in the future, and provides further encouragement to use the module system.
The module system in Lean has been available for over 6 months. Adopting it brings significant benefits (on e.g. the amount of required RAM, or more fine-grained rebuilding), so encouraging it seems useful. At also signals an intent for mathlib to require the use of the module system: future versions of Mathlib might drop support for certain features that require non-module-system libraries.
For example, the simpNF linter currently does not assume the module system is enabled, in the future it might assume that and stop working in libraries that do not use the module system.
This PR has been [announced on Zulip](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/113486-General-announcements/topic/Mathlib.20requiring.20the.20use.20of.20the.20module.20system/with/623623560) before.

ci(build_fork.yml):  supersede fork CI runs by PR head sha instead of arrival order (#43955)
This PR addresses a race condition reported at [#mathlib4 > [pre-commit.ci lite] cancelling CI](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/.5Bpre-commit.2Eci.20lite.5D.20cancelling.20CI/with/623673003). We narrow `build_fork.yml`'s `concurrency` block to runs on the same commit and add a `guard` job that picks the surviving fork run by comparing against the PR's live head sha, rather than by the order GitHub created the runs in.
<details><summary>Details of the race</summary>
When two pushes to a PR occur in quick succession, sometimes the CI for the HEAD commit is triggered before CI for the previous commit starts, causing `cancel-in-progress` to cancel CI for the HEAD commit, causing the CI to get stuck until a manual re-trigger or another push. Example: on #43646, the run for commit `d046ac32` (committed 22:42:59) was created at 22:43:03 and [cancelled](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/actions/runs/34538806707) one second later by the run for `a201b6db` (committed 22:41:49), which then [reported the PR's status](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/actions/runs/34538807811) for a 70-second-stale commit.
</details>
The new guard job skips the build when its sha is no longer the PR head, and otherwise cancels the branch's other in-flight runs. Cancelling rather than skipping the build keeps a superseded run's conclusion at cancelled, matching what the concurrency group produced before, so the `workflow_run` workflows downstream of this one need no changes. We make the guard step block until GitHub cancels the job since the cancel API is asynchronous. The guard fails open: an API error or a failure of `guard` itself builds anyway so a mistake costs a duplicate build rather than a PR with no CI. Never dispatching stale builds saves roughly what superseded runs now cost by living ~30-40s longer, so this should be roughly neutral with respect to runner usage.

chore(MeasureTheory): generalize hypotheses to `NullMeasurableSet` (#42924)
This PR generalizes many statements in `Mathlib.MeasureTheory` from `MeasurableSet s` to `NullMeasurableSet s μ`.
This is particularly useful for lemmas around uniform integrability. A few technical statements which existed only to work around issues of measurability are deprecated thanks to this: `MemLp.eLpNorm_indicator_le_of_meas`, `UniformIntegrable.spec'`, `MemLp.uniformIntegrable_of_identDistrib_aux`. This PR is a preliminary (and necessary)  work before a much more thorough refactor of `MeasureTheory.Function.UniformIntegrable`.
I have chosen to change the hypotheses in place (generalizing the lemmas) instead of adding variants with the new hypothesis, in order to limit quasi-duplicates. There are some limits to this strategy, and a few lemmas have now both `MeasurableSet` and `NullMeasurableSet` versions:
* either if the `MeasurableSet` version was tagged as `simp`;
* or `integrable_indicator_iff₀`, `setLIntegral_congr_fun_ae₀`, `setLIntegral_congr_fun₀`, `setLIntegral_eq_zero₀`, `lintegral_add_compl₀`, `setLIntegral_compl₀`.
The latter 6 lemmas account for the largest potential downstream effects of this PR. If I did not keep the former versions of these 6 lemmas, this PR would have affected five time as many files, including files in e.g. `Geometry` or `NumberTheory`. It seems reasonable that, for quality of life purposes, we keep a few files with `MeasurableSet` hypotheses which are widely used in settings where measurability is essentially a given.
Edit: Implementation note: Some lemmas (e.g. `UniformIntegrable.spec`) were previously proved in two steps. First a version for `Measurable`/`StronglyMeasurable` functions (in this instance, this is lemma `UniformIntegrable.spec'`), then a weakening of the measurability hypotheses. This PR makes it convenient to prove directly the more general version of these lemmas. In these case, I have put the more general lemmas (`UniformIntegrable.spec`) before, deduced the weaker version (`UniformIntegrable.spec'`) from it, and deprecated the latter. This strategy, however, makes the git diff somewhat annoying to read.

feat: `OrderSupSet` (#38328)
This PR introduces `OrderSupSet` and `OrderInfSet`, which are typeclasses expressing that `sSup` (resp., `sInf`) returns the least upper bound (resp., the greatest lower bound) of a set whenever one exists.
This allows us to prove properties about the `sSup` of specific sets (such as `∅`, singletons, finite sets, and `univ`) without any typeclasses asserting the existence of LUBs. For example, `sSup ∅ = ⊥` holds for any type equipped with `OrderBot` `OrderSupSet`, no longer requiring typeclasses like `ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrderBot`.
For a general set `s`, this gives a uniform way to extend results about `IsLUB s a → motive a` to `motive (sSup s)`, `motive (⨆ i, f i)`, `motive (a ⊔ b)`, etc., which allows proof reuse for basic API such as [`csSup_insert`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Order/ConditionallyCompleteLattice/Basic.html#csSup_insert), [`iSup_insert`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Order/CompleteLattice/Basic.html#iSup_insert), and [`sSup_insert`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Order/CompleteLattice/Basic.html#sSup_insert) and downstream code like [`csSup_add`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Group/Pointwise/CompleteLattice.html#csSup_add), [`sSup_add`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Group/Pointwise/CompleteLattice.html#sSup_add), and [`sup_add`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Group/Lattice.html#sup_add).
Furthermore, this allows us to refactor incrementally, reducing the dependency of results about various completeness typeclasses on the specific implementation of `sSup`.

feat(cache): record transport fields on a failed transfer (#44048)
`Get cache` failed 6 of 260 master and staging runs in the week to 2026-09-21. curl receives HTTP 200, then the connection stops mid-body. The log records only this:
```
6033dea46cb996d6.ltar.2212.part: Transfer failed (error code: 200) (curl exit code: 55): Send failure: Broken pipe
```
The line omits how far the body got and which edge served it. curl can report both, so append them:
```
... (curl exit code: 56): Recv failure: Connection reset by peer [bytes=4096/1421777 cf_ray=a3f27b336fa59434-EZE cf_cache_status=HIT http_version=1.1 time_total=0.000788]
```
`bytes` gives the truncation point against the size `content-length` promised, so `bytes=0/1421777` means nothing arrived. `cf_ray` names the Cloudflare data center in its suffix and finds the request in Cloudflare's own logs. `cf_cache_status` says whether the edge cache served the body. Each value describes curl's final attempt, because `--retry` hides the earlier ones.
curl's `%{json}` report carries no response headers. The get path's write-out is that report, then each header value after a 0x1F separator. `monitorCurl` splits the line at the first 0x1F (`splitWriteOut`) and parses only the report. JSON allows no raw control character other than whitespace, so the report always ends at the first separator. The report is the same input as on master, so the verdict, rename and count logic do not change. Only the failure message reads the header values.
The header values stay outside the JSON on purpose. curl writes a header value unescaped, so a value with a quote inside a JSON object makes the line unparseable. `monitorCurl` would then drop that transfer, and the download would be lost. `%{header_json}` would let curl escape the values. It prints every response header, and it has the same version floor. The separator keeps the line short and keeps curl's report as the only parsed input.
The upload path shares `monitorCurl` and keeps its `%{json}` write-out. Its failure lines gain `bytes`, `http_version` and `time_total`, and carry no `cf-*` pair. `bytes` follows the direction, because curl reports the error response body in `size_download`: a read counts `size_download`, a write counts `size_upload`.
`%header{…}` needs curl 7.84. curl 7.83 shipped it as experimental only. `validateCurl` downloads the static curl below 7.84. It accepted 7.81 before, and Ubuntu 22.04 ships 7.81. On another platform, an older curl prints `%header{…}` as literal text, and that text appears only in a failure line.
Only the failure line changes. Transfer behavior stays the same.
Tested with `monitorCurl` against a local server:
- A full 200 body with the headers `cf-ray: abc"\<0x1F>def-EZE` and `cf-cache-status: HIT"` is delivered and renamed.
- A body truncated after 4096 bytes, with `cf-*` headers, gives a failure line like the one above.
- A truncated body without `cf-*` headers gives `[bytes=4096/100000 http_version=1.1 time_total=0.001219]`.
`Cache/Test.lean` adds three tests:
- `test_splitWriteOut` checks that the report ends at the first 0x1F, also when a header value carries a quote or a 0x1F.
- `test_curlGetWriteOut_real_curl` runs the installed curl on a `file://` copy to a file name with a 0x1F and a quote. On Windows the name is plain, because the file system rejects both characters. The report parses back to the same name. The test skips a curl older than 7.84.
- `test_transferDiagnostics` checks the suffix for a download with all headers, a download without `cf-*` headers or `content-length`, and an upload.
If the separator changes to a quote, 7 of the new checks fail. `lake build cache cache-test` is clean, and `lake exe cache-test` passes on Linux and Windows.
The next failure in CI shows where the body stopped and which data center served it.

feat(Translate): better `relevant_arg` heuristic (#43801)
This PR improves the heuristic around `relevant_arg` that `to_dual` and `to_additive` use. Currently, the we eagerly set `(relevant_arg := 1)` whenever we cannot find any relevant argument. This is problematic in a setting where there really should be no relevant argument, such as for `ComplexShape`.
After this PR, we only default to `(relevant_arg := 1)` for types (i.e. anything whose type is `Sort _`). For terms that aren't types, we instead purely rely on the algorithm that determines the relevant argument (which was added in #35318). In order for this algorithm to work in all cases, `relevant_arg` needs to be set on all relevant types. This includes some types that are dual to themselves, like `LE` and `LinearOrder`, and hence do not have a `to_dual` attribute (and hence also don't have a `relevant_arg`). To fix this, I added the following trick: when we add a translation for a class projection or class constructor, and if that class has no translation, then we first add a translation from that class to itself.
As a result, classes like `LE` and `LinearOrder` are now part of the translation dictionary, and are being translated into themselves.

fix(Geometry/Manifold): restore the Hausdorff hypothesis in `NonemptyDiffeomorphSphere` (#43606)
`ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv.NonemptyDiffeomorphSphere M n` (the smooth Poincaré conjecture for `M` in dimension `n`) has no Hausdorff hypothesis. As stated it is false in every positive dimension. One can construct a non-Hausdorff counter-example by taking `𝕊ⁿ` as the one-point compactification of `ℝⁿ` and glue a second copy of the open half-space `B = {x₀ < 1}` onto `𝕊ⁿ` along the smaller open half-space `A = {x₀ < 0}`. 
A Lean proof of `¬ NonemptyDiffeomorphSphere M (n + 1)` for this `M` compiles against Mathlib.
The variable-inclusion backport #15607 removed `[T2Space M]` from the `variable` line and added it to each `proof_wanted` in the file, but not to this `def`, which silently lost it.

fix: fix `cfc_congr` lemmas (#43689)
#43028 introduced a regression in `norm_cast` due to adding an `@[congr]` lemma for `cfc` and `cfcₙ` which did not vary all arguments. This causes the following call to `norm_cast` to fail to close the goal. What happens is that on the LHS, the current `cfc_congr'` lemma causes `norm_cast` to visit the function, but *skip* the argument `((n : A) + m)`, leaving it as `↑n + ↑m`. On the RHS, because nothing needs to happen to the function, it acts on the `((n : A) + m)`, turning it into `↑(n + m)`. Another call to `norm_cast` then closes the goal because it does the same thing to the LHS now.
```lean
module
public import Mathlib.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Basic
example {A : Type*} [CStarAlgebra A] (n m : ℕ) :
    cfc (fun x : ℝ ↦ (x : ℂ).re) ((n : A) + m) = cfc (fun x : ℝ ↦ x) ((n : A) + m) := by
  norm_cast
```
The fix is to update the `cfc_congr'` lemma to vary all the arguments, as with, for example, `Finset.sum_congr`:
```lean
@[congr]
lemma cfc_congr' {f g : R → R} {a b : A} (hab : a = b) (hfg : ∀ x ∈ spectrum R b, f x = g x) :
    cfc f a = cfc g b := by
  subst hab
  exact cfc_congr hfg
```

chore: use simp instead of norm_num where simp suffices (#43035)
This PR replaces `norm_num` with `simp` at 226 call sites where `simp` already closes the goal on its own.
Most of these are `(by norm_num)` discharging a trivial side condition, for example `pow_le_pow_of_le_one (by norm_num) (by norm_num)`, `pow_pos (by norm_num) _`, or `logb_le_logb (b := 2) (by norm_num) _`. `norm_num` runs the full default simp set and then dispatches its extensions on every subterm it visits, so where `simp` suffices the extension dispatch is pure overhead.
The motivation is readability rather than speed.

Building on the API from #41651, prove some results on the maximal subgroups of nilpotent groups and their `p`-group consequences:

feat(Algebra/Polynomial/Sturm): sturm sequences (#43954)
This PR defines `Polynomial.sturmSeq p q`, the Sturm sequence (signed remainder sequence) of two
polynomials over a field: the list `[p, q, -(p % q), …]` of successive negated remainders, ending at
the last nonzero one. It also proves its basic API:
* `sturmSeq_cons`, `sturmSeq_zero`, `sturmSeq_zero_right`, `sturmSeq_eq_nil_iff`: unfolding and
  degenerate cases;
* `mem_sturmSeq_self`, `head?_sturmSeq`, `zero_notMem_sturmSeq`: membership facts;
* `dvd_of_mem_sturmSeq`: every common divisor of `p` and `q` divides every entry;
* `sturmSeq_mul_left`: `sturmSeq (r * p) (r * q) = (sturmSeq p q).map (r * ·)` for `r ≠ 0`.
It also adds `Polynomial.neg_mod` and `Polynomial.mul_mod_mul_left` to `FieldDivision.lean`, used
in the proof of `sturmSeq_mul_left`.
This is the second PR of a series formalizing the Sturm–Tarski theorem, following #43783 
(`List.signVariations`). The development is a port of Wenda Li's Isabelle/AFP entry. The remaining
parts (local sign of a polynomial to the right of a point, the Cauchy index, and the theorem
itself) will follow in separate PRs. See also #43512.
The definition and the original proofs were written by hand. Claude Code (Fable 5.1) was used to
simplify part of the proofs and to review the code.

fix(Tactic/GCongr): make `shake` see `gcongr`'s extension dependencies (#43881)
This PR makes `shake` aware of two `gcongr` dependencies:
- `shake` currently proposes dropping `Mathlib.Tactic.GCongr` from `Mathlib/Tactic/GRewrite.lean`, which makes `Mathlib.Tactic.GCongr.imp_mono` unavailable and breaks proofs using `(p ∨ q) → (p' ∨ q)` by `gcongr`. `GRewrite.lean` imports that module only in order to pass the lemma set on to `grw` users, and there is no use site there to record anything at, so we add a `shake: keep`. At the moment all downstream modules reach this by another path, so this is a purely preventative step.
- `@[gcongr_forward]` extensions are metaprograms that never reach a proof term, so every site that runs one now records it, in the way that `simp` and `grind` already do at their use sites. There are two such sites: `MVarId.gcongrForward`, and `grw`'s own forward-discharge loop in `Mathlib/Tactic/GRewrite/Core.lean`.
(`@[gcongr]` lemmas need no additional recording, because applied lemmas are in the proof term, and `attribute [gcongr]` on an imported declaration records an indirect module use that `shake` folds in from that same constant.)

Inclusion parameters and extensions live in environment extensions, so the dependency on the registering module has to be recorded by hand to be visible to shake. #43784 does this for families (`getInclusionFamily?` records `InclusionFamily.ref`) and `getInclusion/HypothesisExtMatches` does it for extensions, but both record against the module that *invokes* the tactic, leaving the case of modules that exist only to re-export a family together with its extensions. For example, `Extension/IntervalDyadicReal/Tactic.lean` declares only `syntax` and `macro_rules`, so its imports of `Extension.Core.Core`, `..IntervalDyadicReal.Rational` and `..IntervalDyadicReal.Hypotheses` look unused to shake. However, pruning them would break every user of `dyadic_interval` since `Rational` was the path to `Mathlib.Basic.Real.Basic`.
The same hole exists for parameters: `Core/Elab.lean` reads `inclusionParamExt` when elaborating `[prec := 12]` without recording anything, so a file using `prec` has an untraced dependency on `..IntervalDyadicReal.Rational`, and one using `binSplit` on `..BinarySplit`.
This PR adds `DiscrTreeExt.recordRegisteringModule`, wrapping `Lean.recordExtraRevUseOfCurrentModule`, and `EnvExt.register`, which pairs it with the extension update so the two cannot drift apart. Putting it in the shared `DiscrTreeExt` API means other tactics migrated onto it (see the TODO there) inherit the fix.

feat(RingTheory): define Frobenius equations (`Coalgebra.IsFrobenius`) (#27493)
A coalgebra with an algebra structure `A` is said to be Frobenius when it satisfies the Frobenius equation:
`(id ⊗ mul) ∘ assoc ∘ (comul ⊗ id) = comul ∘ mul = (mul ⊗ id) ∘ assoc.symm ∘ (id ⊗ comul)`,
which in diagrams looks like
```
|    |                           |    |
|    μ           |   |           μ    |
|   / \           \ /           / \   |
 \ /   |    =    δ ∘ μ    =    |   \ /
  δ    |          / \          |    δ
  |    |         |   |         |    |
```
where `μ` stands for multiplication and `δ` for comultiplication.
It suffices to show that the left and right diagrams are equal, i.e.,
`(id ⊗ mul) ∘ assoc ∘ (comul ⊗ id) = (mul ⊗ id) ∘ assoc.symm ∘ (id ⊗ comul)`, so this is the only equality in the class.
Because of how long and complicated the names would be, we add abbreviations for the left and right equations, `IsFrobenius.left` and `IsFrobenius.right`. So the Frobenius equation is literally `left_eq_right : IsFrobenius.left = IsFrobenius.right`.
A Frobenius coalgebra is necessarily finite and projective. Also, the bilinear form `(LinearMap.mul R A).compr₂ counit` is nondegenerate and bijective.
A `Bialgebra R A` that is Frobenius must have `R` isomorphic to `A`.

fix(Tactic/Inclusion): record the module registering an inclusion family (#43784)
This PR records the declaration a `registerInclusionFamily` call appears in, so that a module referring to an inclusion family by name acquires a dependency on the module registering that family.
`getInclusionFamily?` already calls `recordExtraModUseFromDecl`, but passes `family.inclusionExt.ext.name`. That name is synthesised by `initializeEnvExt` for `registerScopedEnvExtension`; no constant carries it, so `getModuleIdxFor?` finds nothing and the call silently records nothing. `registerInclusionFamily` already receives the registering declaration as `ref` via `decl_name%`, so storing it on `InclusionFamily` and recording from that gives a name that resolves. This mirrors how core handles the same problem for attributes: `AttributeImplCore` carries a `ref : Name := by exact decl_name%`, and `Lean.Elab.Attributes` records `recordExtraModUseFromDecl (isMeta := true) impl.ref`.
The visible symptom is in `Mathlib/Tactic/Inclusion/Extension/Core/Core.lean`, which reaches the `core` family only through the literal ``​`core``. `lake shake` sees no dependency on `Mathlib.Tactic.Inclusion.Extension.Core.Init` — a module whose entire content is `initialize coreFamily : InclusionFamily ← registerInclusionFamily `core` — and drops the import, after which the file fails to build with ``Unknown inclusion family `core``. That happened in https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/43782, where it is worked around with a `shake: keep` annotation. The `interval_dyadic_real` family is masked from the same problem only because its `Init` module also carries instances that are referenced in the ordinary way.
Checked with `set_option trace.extraModUses true` on `Extension/Core/Core.lean`: before, no recording mentions `Extension.Core.Init`; after, it records `Mathlib.Tactic.Inclusion.Extension.Core.Init of Inclusion.coreFamily`.
